title: Lung abscess (pus pocket in the lung)

items: A lung abscess is a cavity of pus in the lung tissue.
It is most often caused by inhaling food, drink, or saliva into the lungs.
A cough that may bring up foul-smelling sputum (mucus).
Chest X-ray and CT scan of the chest.
Sputum culture, including anaerobic culture (for germs that do not need oxygen) if possible.
Antibiotics are chosen by your doctor based on the cultures.
Some people need drainage or surgery.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Tell your team if you have trouble swallowing or coughing with meals.
Keep up any dental and swallowing care you are advised to have.
Repeat chest X-rays or CT scans show how the abscess is healing.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Coughing up large amounts of blood
Breathlessness at rest, or fever with confusion
